ingestion.source_rule: Keep the source, underlying reported item and conclusion as different records. A mirror, derived image or OCR row inherits its parent’s evidentiary origin.
ingestion.agent_task: Build the incident and investigation timelines. Trace every claim to a source locator, preserve stated limitations, and test the dossier by disabling the disk-metadata lead and checking which independent streams still support attribution. Avoid guessing missing raw evidence.

evidence.description: KSAS-TV received the February 16, 2005 mailing described as Communication 11. The prosecution reports that Detective Dana Gouge collected the envelope, which held the purple diskette and accompanying items.
evidence.locator: PDF p. 42, This Is a Test
evidence.limitation: The filing describes the initial transfer. Exhibit intake logs, full chain-of-custody forms, and the original envelope were not located as downloadable items.

evidence.description: The prosecution reports that Detective Robert Stone examined the disk, found a valid file named Test A.RTF, and observed references to Dennis and Christ Lutheran Church in document properties.
evidence.limitation: Sources describe disk properties and a deleted file differently. The disk image, file bytes, exact fields and recovery method remain unverified.

evidence.description: The verified Internet Archive capture lists Dennis Rader as congregation president on the church’s people page. The capture predates the KSAS mailing.
evidence.limitation: Confirms the public listing. By itself it cannot identify the document’s editor or the sender.

evidence.description: The state filing describes Stone’s online lookup following the disk examination. The lookup returned the church association and generated the named suspect lead.
evidence.locator: PDF p. 42, Disk examination and website lookup
evidence.limitation: The shared given name and church are attribution clues. A separate evidence stream is needed to corroborate the person’s involvement.

evidence.description: The prosecution describes January 8 store security video showing a dark SUV that could have been a Jeep Cherokee. After the disk lead, detectives reported seeing a similar vehicle in Rader’s driveway.
evidence.limitation: The person in the store tape was reported unidentifiable. The description supports a vehicle-type comparison only. Original video was not located in the reviewed public sources.

evidence.description: The state’s filing quotes April 2004 county lab findings linking profiles from evidence in the Otero, Fox, and Wegerle cases to a common unknown male contributor.
evidence.locator: PDF pp. 42–43, County lab findings continued on the next page

citations.section: County lab findings continued on the next page

evidence.limitation: The conclusions use inclusion and exclusion language. Underlying electropherograms and original county reports were not acquired.

evidence.description: A court-authorized family reference was delivered to KBI on February 22, 2005. The prosecution reports that the Otero-scene profile could not be excluded as a biological parent of the reference contributor.
evidence.locator: PDF p. 42, Reference obtained by court order
evidence.limitation: A kinship comparison is an investigative lead. Its strength and methods require the underlying laboratory report.

evidence.description: The prosecution separately describes oral swabs taken from Rader after arrest. It reports KBI and county laboratory comparisons with earlier crime-scene profiles, including the Otero swabs.
evidence.limitation: Preserve the source’s profile-specific distinctions and reported match or non-exclusion language. The packet contains the filed description of those comparisons.

evidence.description: The prosecution places the arrest on February 25, 2005. Police publicly announced the arrest the following day.
evidence.limitation: Dates distinguish taking custody from the public announcement.

evidence.description: The state describes a recorded law-enforcement interview after the arrest. ABC publishes an excerpt of that interview.
evidence.limitation: The public excerpt is edited. The full recording and an official time-coded transcript were not located.

evidence.description: The state describes binders, writings, communications and other media seized from Rader’s Park City office. It reports originals or full-sized versions of multiple communications in the collection.
evidence.limitation: The inventory is a reported account. A described office disk should not be merged with the disk mailed to KSAS.

evidence.description: The released FBI Lab report records that no detectable DNA was recovered from the tested flap area of the October 2004 envelope specimen Q184.
evidence.locator: PDF pp. 110–111, December 6, 2004 DNA Analysis Unit I report, lab 041015012 PO MD

citations.section: December 6, 2004 DNA Analysis Unit I report, lab 041015012 PO MD

evidence.limitation: The negative result belongs to the tested area of Q184. It does not resolve DNA results from unrelated crime-scene specimens.

evidence.description: An FBI questioned-document report says typewriting on specimens Q184–Q186 was inconsistent with previously submitted documents.
evidence.limitation: This comparison is limited to the submitted items and typewriting comparison described on those pages.

evidence.description: A Kansas Supreme Court opinion records that a different man was publicly speculated about during the investigation and cleared by DNA testing in December 2004.
evidence.locator: PDF pp. 4–5, Factual background, broadcast and testing
evidence.limitation: The court opinion describes this as a cleared lead. No same-person or guilt edge should be attached to that person.

evidence.description: The Complaint/Information sets out ten first-degree murder counts and identifies the charged victims.
evidence.locator: PDF pp. 1–5, Counts One through Ten
evidence.limitation: The complaint records the state’s allegations at filing. Refer to the plea and judgment for adjudication.

evidence.description: On June 27, 2005 the district court accepted guilty pleas on all ten first-degree murder counts.
evidence.limitation: The transcript establishes plea and adjudication. It does not independently validate every forensic method described in the prosecution filing.

evidence.description: The court imposed ten consecutive life sentences in August 2005. The signed judgment records the court’s order.
evidence.locator: PDF pp. 3–4, Sentences on Counts One through Ten

citations.section: Sentences on Counts One through Ten

evidence.limitation: The signed journal entry in this packet was filed October 31. Sentencing and filing are separate events.

evidence.description: The court’s order directed destruction of certain investigation swabs, except swabs identifying Rader used in his arrest and conviction, and deferred disposition of other evidence pending appeal and further order.
evidence.locator: PDF pp. 1–2, Court findings and order
evidence.limitation: This is the court’s 2005 direction. The later exhibit inventory and status of particular items remain unverified.

evidence.description: The prosecution records that the Wichita Eagle handed renewed BTK correspondence to investigators in March 2004. Later filings and the FBI case study describe a series of communications before the arrest.
evidence.locator: PDF p. 28, Bill Thomas Killman section

citations.section: FBI investigative summary of resumed contact

evidence.limitation: Record receipt, send and publication dates separately. The underlying full packet of original communications was not located.

evidence.description: The UNT archive dates this news B-roll to the May 3 arraignment. Exterior footage and broadcast close-ups of documents appear in the clip.
evidence.limitation: The clip provides contemporaneous visual context. Individual depicted objects need verification from the exhibit or archive shot list.

evidence.description: KDOC’s photo view identifies the person depicted as Dennis Rader.
evidence.limitation: Portrait for identification and context. Photograph date is unspecified on the image page.

evidence.description: The prosecution describes the dispatch call reporting Nancy Fox’s death. The early investigative timeline and later reporting refer to a recorded call.
evidence.limitation: The original dispatch recording and dispatch log were not acquired.

evidence.description: The prosecution’s evidence summary describes the RTF and accompanying cards and jewelry as parts of the same February 16 mailing.
evidence.limitation: The inventory gives case-level context. It leaves item-level chain of custody and the file’s original hash unverified.

hypotheses.statement: The mailed disk generated a lead pointing to Dennis Rader through a public church listing.
hypotheses.limitation: The archive independently confirms the listing. The original disk and exact location of the recovered strings remain unverified.

hypotheses.statement: Rader was associated with the forensic profiles cited in the Otero, Fox, and Wegerle investigation.
hypotheses.limitation: The familial comparison, Rader’s own reference swabs, and cross-incident comparison answer different questions. The public filing summarizes each.

hypotheses.statement: The early surveillance image alone could identify Rader.
hypotheses.limitation: The filing describes an unidentifiable individual and an uncertain vehicle identification.

hypotheses.statement: The court adjudicated all ten first-degree murder counts.
